To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) aggressive and non-agressive adolescents have a common parenting style pattern: authoritative and indulgent styles are always associated with higher self-esteem and lower personal maladjustment than authoritarian or neglectful styles; (b) indulgent style is always associated with the best adjustment outcomes across all the adjustment criteria; and (c) the relationship between parenting and adjustment shows different pattern for aggressive and nonaggressive adolescents.

(1) Aggressive adolescents always have the worst outcomes, (2) Authoritarian and neglectful parenting styles are associated with the worst outcomes, and (3) Indulgent parenting style is associated with the best socialization outcomes.

(1) the parenting styles are associated with self-esteem and maladjustment in a different way depending on the aggressiveness of adolescents; and (2) indulgent parenting style is always associated with the best self-esteem and the lowest personal maladjustment, regardless of the aggressiveness of the adolescent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the parenting styles and their effects on the development of the self-concept and the maladjustment of aggressive and non-agressive adolescents.
the impact that different parenting styles have on the development of aggressive and non-aggressives adolescents.

the relationship between parenting styles and adolescent adjustment and maladjustments, considering the influence of aggressiveness and sex, and also the role of parental strictness and warmth in adolescent socialization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parental warmth is always beneficial for adolescents’ development and that strictness is only beneficial when it goes hand by hand with parental warmth.
parental warmth, regardless of strictness, is the best parenting style to raise adolescents with the best socialization outcomes.

authoritative parenting style is associated with the best socialization outcomes and authoritarian parenting style with the worst outcomes for all the adolescents, regardless of their level of aggressiveness, and that indulgent parenting style is associated to the best outcomes for non-aggressive adolescents but not for aggressive adolescents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the parenting style that combines warmth and strictness (authoritative style) seems to be the best for all the adolescents, but especially for aggressive ones, as it is related with the highest self-esteem and the lowest personal maladjustment.
parental strictness does not seem to have a protective effect against aggressive adolescents, and that parental warmth is always beneficial.
parenting styles are related to adolescent adjustment and maladjustments, and this relationship is moderated by aggressiveness, sex and age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parenting style is a key factor to promote adolescent adjustment, and that the impact of parental style is the same for aggressive and nonaggressive adolescents.
parental warmth is always better for the adolescent than parental strictness.
parental strictness might have a different impact on aggressive and non-agressive adolescents.
